**Proposition.** For any many-body quantum system $H$ acting on $\bigotimes_{i=1}^n \mathcal{H}_i$ with $n \geq N_0$ (where $N_0$ is system-dependent), there exists a functor $F: \mathbf{QSys} \to \mathbf{CollMode}$ mapping the system to a category of collective modes, where objects in $\mathbf{CollMode}$ are operators $\hat{O}$ satisfying $\langle\hat{O}\rangle \neq \sum_i\langle\hat{o}_i\rangle$ for any decomposition $\hat{O} = \sum_i \hat{o}_i$ with $\hat{o}_i$ acting on single-particle subspaces.

**Proof.** Let $\mathcal{H} = \bigotimes_{i=1}^n \mathcal{H}_i$ be a separable Hilbert space with Hamiltonian $H$ that includes interaction terms not expressible as $\sum_i h_i$ where each $h_i$ acts only on $\mathcal{H}_i$. We assume the system admits a well-defined thermodynamic limit as $n \to \infty$, the ground state $|\Psi_0\rangle$ is non-degenerate, and the interaction strength exceeds a critical threshold ensuring non-perturbative effects.

We first construct the category $\mathbf{QSys}$ of many-body quantum systems with objects $(\mathcal{H}, H, n)$ and morphisms given by unitary transformations preserving particle number. For each system $S \in \mathbf{QSys}$ with $n \geq N_0$, we form the reduced density matrix $\rho^{(k)} = \text{Tr}_{n-k}(|\Psi_0\rangle\langle\Psi_0|)$ for $k$-particle subsystems.

By the subadditivity of von Neumann entropy and the presence of entanglement in interacting ground states, we have $S(\rho^{(k)}) > S(\rho_1^{\otimes k})$ where $S$ denotes the von Neumann entropy. This inequality demonstrates that the $k$-particle subsystem cannot be described as a product of single-particle states.

Applying the Gibbs ensemble formalism, we identify emergent degrees of freedom through the partition function $Z = \text{Tr}(e^{-\beta H})$. By Gibbs Ensemble Theory, this connects microscopic and macroscopic descriptions of the system.

We now identify collective excitation operators $\hat{O}_\alpha$ as those creating states $|\psi_\alpha\rangle = \hat{O}_\alpha|\Psi_0\rangle$ satisfying $\langle\psi_\alpha|\sum_i P_i|\psi_\alpha\rangle < \epsilon$ for projectors $P_i$ onto single-particle excitations. This orthogonality condition characterizes the collective nature of these excitations.

[Note: A rigorous construction of morphisms in the $\mathbf{CollMode}$ category and verification of composition rules remains to be established.]

As a concrete example, nuclear systems exhibit the Giant Dipole Resonance, where the collective operator $Q = \sum_i(r_i)_p - \sum_j(r_j)_n$ creates coherent proton-neutron oscillations. This experimentally verified mode demonstrates the physical reality of collective excitations.

We define the functor $F: \mathbf{QSys} \to \mathbf{CollMode}$ by mapping $(\mathcal{H}, H, n) \mapsto \{\hat{O}_\alpha\}$. [Note: Full verification of functoriality conditions requires showing that $F$ preserves composition and identity morphisms.]

Finally, the collective modes satisfy $\langle\hat{O}_\alpha\rangle \neq \sum_i\langle\hat{o}_i\rangle$ for any single-particle decomposition. This follows from the orthogonality condition established above and the entanglement structure revealed by the entropy inequality.

This completes the proof. $\square$
